question: Question linked to image nº17 A young patient of 22 years of age is referred to us from Primary Care. He is originally from Jamaica and has been living in Spain for five months. The reason for consulting the family doctor was a feeling of tiredness. As a background, he explains some pains of several years of evolution in various joints, of moderate intensity, without inflammatory signs, which had not been studied in his country. The clinical examination shows pale mucous membranes and a painful ulcerated lesion in the leg, of three years of evolution, for which he had not consulted. I did not remember any local trauma. The analytical sample shows a Hb of 7.6 g / dL, reticulocytes 417,000 / uL, Hto 22.8%, leukocytes 13.540 / uL, with 51% of neutrophils and 36% of lymphocytes, platelets 286,000 / uL, bilirubin 2.12 mg / dL, (direct 0.4 mg / dL) and lactate dehydrogenase 318 U / L (vn <190 U / L). A basic study of coagulation is within normal ranges. The chest radiograph is normal, as well as an Eco-Doppler of the lower extremities. What type of anemia would you suspect before starting the corresponding confirmatory studies?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pale mucous membranes" -> "suggests possible anemia" -> "low hemoglobin of 7.6 g/dL" -> "indicates significant anemia" -> "elevated reticulocyte count of 417,000/uL" -> "suggests compensatory response to anemia" -> "joint pains without inflammatory signs" -> "possible chronic condition" -> "ulcerated lesion in leg" -> "could indicate underlying disease" -> "elevated bilirubin and LDH" -> "suggests hemolysis" -> "sickle cell anemia is common in Jamaican population" -> "consider sickle cell anemia" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Pale mucous membranes" -> "indicates anemia" -> "hemoglobin of 7.6 g/dL" -> "severe anemia" -> "reticulocyte count elevated" -> "suggests bone marrow response" -> "joint pains present" -> "could indicate chronic disease" -> "ulcerated lesion present" -> "possible chronic infection or disease" -> "elevated bilirubin and LDH" -> "suggests hemolysis" -> "autoimmune hemolytic anemia possible" -> "consider autoimmune hemolytic anemia" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Pale mucous membranes" -> "indicates anemia" -> "low hemoglobin of 7.6 g/dL" -> "suggests significant anemia" -> "reticulocyte count elevated" -> "indicates bone marrow response" -> "joint pains without inflammation" -> "could suggest chronic disease" -> "ulcerated lesion present" -> "could indicate chronic infection" -> "elevated bilirubin and LDH" -> "suggests hemolysis" -> "chronic disease could explain anemia" -> "consider anemia due to chronic disease" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Pale mucous membranes" -> "indicates anemia" -> "hemoglobin of 7.6 g/dL" -> "significant anemia" -> "reticulocyte count elevated" -> "suggests compensatory response" -> "joint pains present" -> "could indicate chronic disease" -> "ulcerated lesion present" -> "could indicate chronic infection" -> "normal coagulation studies" -> "less likely iron deficiency anemia" -> "consider anemia due to iron deficiency" -> 60%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms of fatigue, pale mucous membranes, and a painful ulcerated lesion, along with laboratory findings indicating anemia (Hb 7.6 g/dL) and elevated bilirubin (2.12 mg/dL) and LDH (318 U/L). The elevated reticulocyte count suggests a compensatory response to anemia, which is often seen in hemolytic processes. Given the patient's background from Jamaica, where sickle cell disease is prevalent, and the chronic joint pain without inflammatory signs, sickle cell anemia is a strong consideration. The ulcerated lesion could also be related to sickle cell disease complications. Therefore, the most likely type of anemia before further confirmatory studies would be anemia due to sickle cells.
